tagline: Two cops. One case. Several misunderstandings.
about: A Hong Kong inspector and a loudmouth LA cop team up to find a kidnapped girl.

    StartersConsulate spring rollsCrisp pastry rolls with cabbage, carrot, shiitake and glass noodles.How to make it30g glass noodles120g cabbage, shredded1 carrot60g shiitake mushrooms1 tsp neutral oil1 tsp light soy sauce8 spring rolls of pastry sheets1 tsp plain flour1 L vegetable oil, for frying40ml sweet chilli sauceSoak the glass noodles in hot water, drain and cut short.Shred the cabbage, grate the carrot and slice the shiitake.Stir-fry the vegetables in oil, add the noodles and soy and stir briefly. Cool completely.Divide among the pastry sheets, roll tightly and seal with a paste of flour and water.Fry in 180°C oil until golden.Serve with sweet chilli sauce.Carter's hot wingsCrisp baked wings in hot butter sauce with cooling ranch dip.How to make it600g chicken wings1/2 tsp salt25g butter35ml hot sauce80g sour cream20g mayonnaise1 tbsp chopped chives1/4 tsp garlic powder1 tsp lemon juicePat the wings dry and season with salt.Bake on a rack at 220°C, turning halfway, until crisp and at least 74°C inside.Mix the sour cream, mayonnaise, chives, garlic powder and lemon juice for the ranch dip.Melt the butter with the hot sauce and toss through the wings.MainsFoo Chow noodlesWide rice noodles wok fried with beef, sprouts and spring onion.How to make it400g beef rump2 tbsp light soy sauce1 tsp cornflour1 tsp sesame oil600g fresh wide rice noodles2 tbsp neutral oil150g bean sprouts3 spring onions1 tbsp dark soy sauceThinly slice the beef and marinate with the light soy, cornflour and sesame oil.Gently separate the noodles.Stir-fry the beef in two batches in a hot wok and set aside.Fry the noodles in more oil.Add the bean sprouts, sliced spring onions and soy sauces. Return the beef and toss over high heat until piping hot.Carter's fried chicken and mac plateFried chicken and greens. Chen: no soul foodHow to make itAs written, serves 4Buttermilk fried chicken with a crunchy spiced crust, smoky braised greens with ham hock and a bubbling baked mac and cheese.Soak 1kg chicken pieces overnight in 500ml buttermilk with hot sauce and salt.Simmer 1 smoked ham hock in 1.5 litres water for 1 hour, add 2 bunches shredded kale or silverbeet and 2 tbsp vinegar and braise 30 minutes.Toss chicken in 250g flour with paprika, garlic powder and pepper, fry at 165°C for 14 minutes.Cook 300g macaroni, stir into a sauce of 40g butter, 40g flour, 600ml milk and 200g cheddar, top with more cheese and bake at 200°C for 20 minutes.SweetsRansom fortune cookiesThin vanilla cookies folded around paper fortunes while still hot.How to make it8 paper fortunes (food-safe strips)2 egg whites50g caster sugar25g butter, melted40g plain flour1/2 tsp vanilla extract1 tbsp waterWrite the fortunes on small clean paper strips.Whisk the egg whites and sugar until foamy and stir in the butter, flour, vanilla and water.Spread two thin circles at a time on a lined tray and bake at 180°C until the edges turn golden.Working quickly while hot, place a fortune in each, fold in half and bend over a mug rim. Cool in muffin-tin cups. Repeat for the rest.Remind everyone to remove the paper before eating.DrinksConsulate lychee and jasmine martiniVodka shaken with chilled jasmine tea, lychee syrup and a squeeze of lime, strained into coupes with a whole lychee dropped in.How to make it1 jasmine tea bag120ml hot water1 tin lychees (565g)160ml vodka80ml lychee syrup (from the tin)1 lime1 tray iceBrew the tea bag in the hot water and cool.Drain the lychees, keeping the syrup.Shake the vodka, tea, lychee syrup and lime juice with ice.Strain into chilled coupes and drop a lychee into each.
